correctness.rationale: The universal response-speed function is strictly concave (explicit positive H double derivative and concave increasing inverse), so strict Jensen forces a positive equivalent-retention derivative for every positive-runoff depth. Existence, boundary limits, strict composite-retention Jensen inequality, high-storm expansion and unique crossing are derived with all quantifiers and inactive-site cases accounted for. Checker tests are supplementary only.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The first-order response identity \(q_P=\Phi_P(q)\) and strict Jensen turn a known finite-class phenomenon into an all-law quantified theorem. At high rainfall the exact limit is \(-(1+\lambda)(\mathbb E S-S(\mathbb E C))<0\), which supplies a mathematically unavoidable bias reversal not reported in accessible abstracts. Because a likely closely related 2016 full analysis was inaccessible, this PASS is provisional and historical-priority risk is material.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Effective CN is an inverse-runoff reformulation of distributed mixture runoff and is not new per se. The new mathematical statement asserts strict increasing equivalent retention at every positive-runoff storm depth for every nondegenerate compact spatial law (not just two classes), plus exactly one sign reversal against arithmetic composite CN. The accessible prior results do not establish those strict global quantifiers. The inaccessible complete Her treatment leaves a priority risk.

value.rationale: A nontrivial general all-storm theorem rules out multiple effective-CN reversals and proves a unique crossover of a commonly used watershed aggregation procedure for any compactly supported heterogeneous landscape. It provides a sharp mathematical benchmark for selecting storm-size ranges and diagnosing composite-CN bias, rather than merely a numerical case or textbook substitution.
